findings.claim: UPHELD. Optional WORKER_HARNESSES plus a future get()/os.environ.get("WORKER_HARNESSES") reader is an undeclared-read against the live closure gate; EXECUTABLE_<NAME> has no MODEL_/EFFORT_ prefix reader, so a declared EXECUTABLE_AGY is an unread declaration. Missing test-facing closure obligation, not unimplemented adapter code. The docstring-only tree at this ref does not currently trip _reads (no get/environ literals; measured). Smallest correction: in the laneconf module contract, name closure() — put WORKER_HARNESSES in tracked ops/lane.conf or EXTERNAL_ENV_KEYS, and add an EXECUTABLE_ prefix provision beside laneconf.py:357-363. No new admission framework.

UPHELD. The amendment forbids relabelling a file value as env:KEY, but dispatch.sh:55-88 saves only the fixed keys plus ${!MODEL_@} and ${!EFFORT_@}. Sourcing a conf that declares WORKER_HARNESSES or EXECUTABLE_* overwrites an exported operator value and keeps the export attribute, so laneconf.worker() would see the file value as env:KEY. Missing named wrapper seam, not unimplemented worker(). Smallest correction: name that dispatch.sh saved_keys restore must include WORKER_HARNESSES and EXECUTABLE_* (or must not source those keys into the process environment). Pin in test_dispatch_wrapper.py.

findings.claim: UPHELD. The amendment claims a generic MODEL_<NAME>/EFFORT_<NAME> family and that absent/empty effort means no effort argv. The named wrapper has a three-arm model case (dispatch.sh:217-223) and effort=${!effort_harness} with no :- under set -u (lines 2, 228-229). Today's hardcoded allowlist at line 177 hides both rungs; replacing it with the loader check the amendment requires exposes them. Contradictory claim about the named seam. Smallest correction: after the job-key rung, a generic MODEL_<NAME> fallback (agy has no code default; empty then launch still requires --model); Claude PLAN/READ stays special-cased; effort final rung is ${!effort_harness:-}.

UPHELD. Intra-document contradiction, not unimplemented refusals. §Refusals (805-834) is the declared table; the amendment adds worker, executable and unsupported-capability only in prose at 102-117. Row 825 still marks write-role-unadmitted as claude; row 829 marks resume-store as a codex or grok resume; launch.py:1088-1090 and 935-948 match those older scopes. The amendment's regression-home list omits tests/test_launch_refusals.py, which already owns those ids. Smallest correction: add the three ids to the table with expected/found/satisfy; re-scope write-role-unadmitted to any harness without a write sandbox (agy until measured); re-scope resume-store to home-isolated resumes including agy; name test_launch_refusals.py in the amendment list.

Rejected: inventing a measured sandbox flag or store path. Isolation already forbids guessing auth/session path; permission/mode tokens already require evidence and unsupported-capability. Smallest correction: name _harness_meta in the adapter table; pin harness.containment to policy for agy (trusted-host, not os); treat sandbox as an unresolved record label that adds no permission/mode argv until measured; isolation.store follows measured sessions.{under,path} and until then unsupported-capability refuses before minting a store. findings.claim: PARTIAL. Missing test-facing injection seam: launch is told to use worker.executable as argv[0] while _argv keeps signature (name, ...) and name also drives per-harness branching (launch.py:495-497). Intra-amendment tension with all three fresh/resume argv persist if PATH-miss refusal and symlink realpath apply to the three defaults. Not a reason to drop executable overrides. findings.claim: REJECTED. Current grok/claude else-branches are unimplemented adapter work the amendment already specifies: agy effort is ['--effort', effort] (CONTRACT.md:72), and _stream must discover only the measured isolated store, never the newest unrelated stream (CONTRACT.md:74). That already contradicts grok's --reasoning-effort and claude's $HOME/.claude glob once the agy branches exist. Requiring exhaustive-match-or-refuse inside every helper is a new admission framework this ruling does not add. Session-mismatch exemption is codex-only today; agy session flags remain unresolved and are already covered by unsupported-capability.

PARTIAL. Independent fake-CLI tests need a candidate argv, and --print/--model/--effort/--disable-slash-commands are in inventory E3. --input-format and --output-format are not in that reading, which only records 'text/json/stream-json output, text/stream-json input'. The amendment's own verify-not-assert rule applies to those two tokens. Not a demonstrated wrong flag; agy --help was not re-run here. Smallest correction: keep the bounded transport list but mark those two flag spellings unresolved, or quote E3's actual input/output words, until a help-line citation exists.
